Title: Diagnosis

Details:
- Test intent:
  - setUp builds:
    - parentOption (-p/--parent) with an argument.
    - childOption1 (-c/--child) and childOption2 (-s/--sub), both with arguments.
    - childGroup named "childOptions" with min=0, max=2, containing childOption1 and childOption2.
    - parentGroup named "parentOptions" with min=1, max=1, containing parentOption and childGroup.
    - Parser is set to use parentGroup as the root.
  - testMultipleChildOptions invokes parser.parse with only the child options: --child test --sub anotherTest. This should satisfy parentGroup’s requirement of exactly one selected among {parentOption, childGroup} because childGroup should count as present when any of its children are present.

- Observed failure mechanism:
  - During parsing, when options are recognized, they are recorded via WriteableCommandLineImpl.addOption(Option).
  - Current implementation:
    - Adds the concrete option to an internal set and maps its triggers to it.
    - Contains a comment “ensure that all parent options are also added” but has no implementation to do so.
  - Consequence:
    - When only child options are provided, WriteableCommandLineImpl marks childOption1 and childOption2 as present but does not mark their parent group (childGroup) as present.
    - Later, the top-level group validation counts how many of its immediate children are present among [parentOption, childGroup]. This presence check is via commandLine.hasOption(child) for each child.
    - parentOption is not present; childGroup is also not marked present (since groups are never added), so the count is 0.
    - This violates parentGroup’s minimum=1 constraint, causing parse to fail with an OptionException. The test, which expects parsing to succeed, therefore fails.

- Code evidence aligning with the bug report:
  - WriteableCommandLineImpl.addOption(Option) only records the specific option and its triggers; it does not propagate presence to ancestors. It even includes a TODO-style comment: “ensure that all parent options are also added”.
  - Parent/group validation logic relies on commandLine.hasOption(child) to determine presence. Since groups are not added to the CommandLine, hasOption(group) returns false, matching the issue report: “Groups are never added to a CommandLine so .hasOption(A) returns false and so it isn't counted.”

- Root cause:
  - Missing propagation of presence in WriteableCommandLineImpl.addOption: when a child option is added, all ancestor “parent” options and groups must also be marked as present. Without this, group min/max constraints that include other groups do not recognize those groups as present even when their children are supplied.

- Why the test fails:
  - The test supplies two child options and expects the child group to count as the one required selection at the top level. Because the group is not marked present in the CommandLine, the top-level group sees zero selections and rejects the command line, failing the test.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
